lines.text: Without approvals you get two bad options. Let agents do anything, or watch every terminal.
An A I agent task board brings each question to you. Here is how Agent R Q does it.
A risky command comes to you as a request, with the exact command. Allow and Deny sit on its card.
Agents can ask with a card too, built on Eh two U I, the open standard.
A button for a choice, a form for the details. One click answers.
Results come back the same way: a chart, or one live card that updates.
A toast finds you on any page. Push, email and Slack reach you with the tab closed.
Trust a task end to end? Turn on Yolo for autonomous task execution.
Every call still goes on the record, marked auto-allowed.
The trajectory keeps every tool call, and who said no.
The timeline says where the time went. Worked, blocked, or waiting on you.
What would you still approve by hand? Tell us in the comments. Agent R Q is open source: try it at Agent R Q dot com.
